liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (3 reviews): Serious primal Dead playing occurs during Lovelight, leading into classic segues; They played a 20-minute Lovelight, followed by a 15-minute version, letting it flow [7][10][11]
- **Dark Star** (1 review): Dark Star features intense moments and notable interaction between Phil and Jerry [6]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): The Eleven is described as excellent, alongside the Lovelight sandwich and Sittin' On Top Of The World [6]

## The recordings

- **gd69-04-27.sbd.cotsman.5070.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 8 songs; 98 min; rated 4.15/5 by 13 [1]. Said about its sound: The recording is ferocious, with TC quite audible throughout the performance [7]

## Around the show

- Listener conversed with a chirping bird outside the window while the song played [2]
- The Dead may have been the first band to perform at this venue [3]
- A photo from inside the Aveda building shows the 4th floor window shape [5]
- The band followed the Bobby Lyle Quintet and local acts, playing one set [10]
- The Labor Temple was the Minneapolis answer to The Fillmore, opening in February 1969 [11]
- The show was on the 3rd floor; the venue is now a parking lot [12]
- The venue's first show was Grateful Dead on February 2, 1969, at minus 25 degrees [12]
- The Grateful Dead returned in April for this show, with the Bobby Lyle Quintet [12]
- This show is considered better than the other performance featured on the Dick's Picks release [6]
- Parts of this show are considered even better than the album Live/Dead [8]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-04-27.sbd.cotsman.5070.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by J. Cotsman and Jeff Krakowka; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: SBD transferred to MR, D, CD, then SHN by J. Cotsman, with thanks to Jeff Krakowka [1]
